title: Mock analysis sheet
subject: English Literature
unit: Summer 2: Unseen poetry (Component 1 Section A); mock
source: Seeded from english-literature/y10 lesson 63 (Mock analysis sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Mock paper. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: Where does the poem turn?
options: 'Next spring, he says, the ground remembers.'
questions.a: B) 'Next spring, he says, the ground remembers.'. The final stanza turns from autumn's ending to the hope of spring.

questions.q: What causes the change in the speaker?
options: the grandmother saying the name whole
questions.a: C) the grandmother saying the name whole. Stanza 2 shows the grandmother's respect, which the speaker later adopts.

questions.q: Which is the best overview sentence?
options: The poet presents the sea as a living mind that leaves and returns by choice.
The poem is about the beach.
questions.a: A) The poet presents the sea as a living mind that leaves and returns by choice.. It sums up the poem's central idea; the others describe surface details.

questions.q: Which pair shows juxtaposition in the poem?
options: the city 'floods in' and 'walks across her without looking down' / the floor that 'knows who made it clean'
questions.a: C) the city 'floods in' and 'walks across her without looking down' / the floor that 'knows who made it clean'. The careless crowd is set against the floor's quiet knowledge of her work.

questions.q: Which is the strongest thesis for question A?
options: Steinbeck presents loneliness as a disease of the system: every outsider is isolated by a society that sets workers against each other.
There are lonely people in the novel.
Of Mice and Men was written in 1937.
questions.a: A) Steinbeck presents loneliness as a disease of the system: every outsider is isolated by a society that sets workers against each other.. It argues a concept and links to context; the others state facts.

questions.q: Which partner works best with Remember for loss?
options: Do not go gentle into that good night
questions.a: B) Do not go gentle into that good night. Both explore death and how the living should respond, so the comparison is rich.

questions.q: in the portal response box, write two analytical paragraphs on how the poet presents change. Starter: 'The poet presents change as...'
questions.a: Two paragraphs: method, short quotation, effect
questions.model: Point: change is presented as tiredness at first | Evidence: 'like old friends with nothing left to say' | Method: simile | Effect: the season feels worn out, gentle rather than harsh

questions.q: write a paragraph on the final stanza's shift in tone
questions.a: A paragraph on the turn

questions.q: comment on the form: three equal stanzas and the effect of the last line
questions.a: A comment on form and the ending

questions.q: Step 2: who speaks, about what, and what changes?
questions.a: a grandchild watching the grandfather prepare the allotment for winter; from ending to hope
questions.model: I do: speaker: 'my grandfather' shows a grandchild; subject: the autumn allotment; change: from tired ending to belief in spring.

questions.q: Annotate 'a robin argues with the rain': method and effect
questions.a: personification; the garden is still lively and defiant

questions.q: in the portal response box, answer: How does the poet present the speaker's feelings about her name?
questions.a: An overview and three developed paragraphs (marked against the AO2 focus list)

questions.q: self-assess with the AO2 focus list and add one improvement
questions.a: One improvement in a different colour

questions.q: comment on the effect of the short sentence 'I was seven.'
questions.a: It is blunt and matter-of-fact; it explains her choice and invites sympathy

questions.q: Plan (5 minutes): overview and three points with quotations
questions.a: A five-minute plan
questions.model: I do: overview: the poem moves from shame to pride; then one point per stanza, each with a short quotation and an effect.

questions.q: in the portal response box, write an overview and two analytical paragraphs on how the poet presents the sea
questions.a: An overview and two paragraphs

questions.q: write the third paragraph on the final stanza's structure
questions.a: A paragraph on the build from whisper to sound

questions.q: offer an alternative reading of 'having made up its mind'
questions.a: For example: the return feels deliberate, even slightly threatening

questions.q: Write an overview sentence for 'Low Tide'
questions.a: For example: The poet presents the sea as a living mind that leaves and returns by choice.
questions.model: I do: what does the whole poem do? It personifies the sea from start to end: a mind that 'goes out to think' and returns 'having made up its mind'.
